articles.summary: Guided by its vision to “solving labor shortages and enriching people and companies,” Uluru Co., Ltd. runs a business centered on CGS (Crowd Generated Service)* and BPO (Business Process Outsourcing). With eight sites nationwide, including subsidiaries, and a workforce built around remote work, Uluru had adopted SaaS tools department by department — but lacked real-time visibility into network traffic and was carrying the vulnerability risk of its VPN appliances. In 2021, the company laid out a grand design for its shift to zero trust. For one of its final milestones — deploying a CASB (Cloud Access Security Broker) — Uluru chose Netskope. The deciding factors were its SaaS visibility, dedicated IP service, and the overall strength of Netskope Private Access (NPA) in retiring VPN altogether. Here’s the story behind how the employee who led the project — with no prior network experience, and with support from those around him — achieved full traffic visibility and VPN retirement across the entire company. *Crowd Generated Service is Uluru’s own business model built around crowd workers.
articles.title: Uluru Uses Netskope CASB to Retire VPN and Achieve Company-Wide Zero Trust
